claims_about_writeup.quote: submission/contribution.md** — method, provenance, and novelty claim.
claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up does describe the method, explains where the direction comes from relative to white-bear steering (provenance), and makes an explicit novelty claim in its 'Where it comes from / novelty' section.

message_source_quote: Reproduced white-bear steering ("think/don't-think") as a control — 0.58 on fit with the same 30 carriers/concepts.
writeup_source_quote: White-bear steering (Raman et al., `papers/raman2026`) showed that a *propositional* stance — "think about X" vs "don't think about X" — lifts implied concepts through the plain J-lens; reproducing it here with the same 30 carriers and 30 concepts scores 0.58 on fit.
rationale: Both documents explicitly name the source as white-bear steering / Raman et al., state that it was reproduced as a control/comparison scoring 0.58 on the fit split with the same 30 carriers and concepts, and claim the submitted method's novelty as steering a distinct 'imagery' axis (cosine ~0.77-0.82 from the think-direction) that outperforms it (0.77 vs 0.58). The write-up adds one extra technical detail (a cosine comparison against the published directed-modulation extraction, ~0.66-0.70) that the message omits, but this is a mechanism/number detail rather than a change in how the source, overlap, or novelty is framed, so the two documents are materially equivalent on source treatment."
